abort.samsung_browser_unavailable: Couldn't reach Samsung's sign-in service. Check the log and try again.

error.invalid_redirect_url: No authorization code found in the URL. Check the URL and try again.
error.code_exchange_failed: Failed to exchange the authorization code. Check your credentials and try again.
error.samsung_login_failed: Samsung rejected the Samsung Account login, so camera pictures can't be enabled. This usually means the Samsung signin client secret is missing or wrong, or the account uses 2-step verification. Clear the three Samsung fields to finish setup without camera pictures; the log has Samsung's exact reply.
error.no_device_found: No Family Hub fridge with a camera was found in this SmartThings account. Enter the fridge's Device ID manually.
error.invalid_image_token: SmartThings rejected this token. Check you copied it fully and that it hasn't expired.
error.samsung_2fa_required: Samsung accepted your password but wants a 2-step verification (SMS) code, which this login can't enter. Turn off 2-step verification in your Samsung account, set up this integration, then turn it back on; or clear the Samsung fields to set up without camera pictures.
error.invalid_samsung_redirect: That doesn't contain the ms-app://… address Samsung sends after sign-in. Copy the whole address or Console message.
error.samsung_browser_failed: Samsung didn't accept the sign-in result. Start setup again for a fresh link; if it keeps failing, check the log for Samsung's reply.

user.title: Choose authentication method
user.description: Samsung deprecated indefinite SmartThings Personal Access Tokens on 2024-12-30 — new PATs expire every 24 hours. Reusing the HA core SmartThings integration's OAuth2 credentials avoids this limit entirely.

standalone_oauth_samsung.title: Standalone SmartThings OAuth — Samsung Account (optional)
standalone_oauth_samsung.description:
Camera pictures need a Samsung identity. Fill in ONE of: a **picture token** (a SmartThings personal access token from https://account.smartthings.com/tokens; expires every 24 hours), or your **Samsung Account** login. Leave all fields empty to skip pictures.

{samsung_signin_client_secret_hint}

oauth.title: Reuse SmartThings OAuth credentials
oauth.description:
Select an existing HA core SmartThings integration to borrow its OAuth2 credentials. Tokens will refresh automatically.

The fridge is found automatically; enter its Device ID only if detection fails (find it at https://my.smartthings.com/advanced/devices).

**Camera pictures** come from a Samsung server that Home Assistant's SmartThings login can't use. To get pictures, choose ONE of:
- **Sign in through Samsung's website** (tick the box): works with 2-step verification and renews itself. You'll get a sign-in link on the next screen.
- **Samsung Account** email + password (+ signin client secret): renews itself, but doesn't work with 2-step verification.
- **Picture token**: a token from https://account.smartthings.com/tokens. Expires every 24 hours.

Leave them all empty to set up without pictures.

samsung_browser.title: Sign in to your Samsung account
samsung_browser.description:
1. On a computer, open Chrome or Edge, press **F12** and select the **Console** tab. Leave it open.
2. In that same tab, open this link and sign in (including the SMS code if Samsung asks):

[Open Samsung sign-in]({sign_in_url})

3. After signing in, the page tries to open an address starting with **ms-app://** and nothing seems to happen. The Console shows a red message like *Failed to launch 'ms-app://…'*. Copy that whole message (or just the ms-app://… address) and paste it below.

If you don't see it in the Console, look in the **Network** tab (tick *Preserve log* and sign in again) for a request starting with ms-app://.

The link works once. If it fails, close this dialog and start setup again for a fresh link.

data.redirect_url: ms-app://… address (or the whole Console message)
